correctness.rationale: For every real p>1 and positive A,B,a<b, an exact derivative identity reduces beta to (p+1)/p times one plus a strictly positive mixing term. The time ratio r=(t+a)/(t+b) grows strictly. Its derivative sign is governed by H(r), whose first term decreases from positive to zero on (0,p/(p+2)) while its second term is strictly increasing and positive; above that interval H<0. Thus there is exactly one possible interior peak, with the exact iff initial-offset and amplitude criteria. At fixed r, x/(1+x)^2<=1/4 with equality at x=1, giving sharp p=2 beta>2 exactly when r<1/3 and hence attainable for positive time iff b/a>3. Exact rational p=2 witnesses and 14412 finite diagnostic assertions were reproduced from checker.py; finite assertions are not the general proof.

originality.rationale: Jachens et al. (2020) covers the qualitative phenomenon of altered recession exponents from nonlinear power-law superposition and receives full credit for that prior result. The newly claimed contribution is strictly the global unique-maximum iff criterion for two equal-power nonlinear stores and the sharp existence condition b/a>3 for instantaneous exponent above two at p=2. No inspected full-text source establishes those exact statements. Historical priority is provisional due to inaccessible 1999 Wittenberg and 2017 Gao full text.

value.rationale: A known ecological/hydrological modeling question is how nonlinear recession components combine; Jachens et al. (2020) show this phenomenon without a sharp global classification. The exact necessary-and-sufficient b/a>3 threshold for two square-law components and unique-peak parameter criterion quantify when observed high local recession exponents are possible at all in that precise model; these are actionable mathematical diagnostics, not a rediscovery of qualitative mixing or an empirical fit.
